errata.old: DropStorage, LogicalDelete, Redact, Truncate x {final>critical, final>none}; HardDelete final>none; Update final>none (10 deltas)
errata.new: DropStorage, HardDelete, LogicalDelete, Redact, Truncate, Update x {final>critical, final>none} (12 deltas)
errata.reason: A.8.2.3 L1 makes a part for each base forbid f, position x and atom a where Lvl_h(x)(a) < tier_b(f), with delta 'L1 level <atom> <tier_b>><tier_h>'. A.8.2.1 unions the deltas, and A.8.3.2 adds the demoted positions, appendEvent among them, to affected. A.4.4.7 and A.8.2.3 [D2] make Lvl include the unit's own complete summary. Under syntax §1, appendEvent has 'effects complete { Append<AuditEvent> }' in AuditStore, which is tier critical, so in the Variant C head HardDelete and Update at appendEvent are protected only by that summary, at critical. Base AppendOnly had them at final. The parts 'L1 level HardDelete<audit::AuditEvent> final>critical' and 'L1 level Update<audit::AuditEvent> final>critical' were missing.

The text names this key only as Variant C's authority loosening. EXAMPLES.md Variant A says 'L1 is implied, since the final forbid still excludes HardDelete and Update', and A.8.2.3 L1 [D17] says 'an atom gained in A that a forbid still blocks is no part'. Under version 7, Variant A therefore raises no loosening of component AuditStore, and the name carried a version 6 reading. The value is unchanged. kernel/test/gen_cases.py (version 6) still uses the old name, and it reads its own scratch copy of the vectors.

errata.old: descends into dict and list; asserts str keys
errata.new: descends into dict, list and tuple; asserts str ASCII keys
errata.reason: A.0.4 and the M0 exit criterion require that vectors.py assert no floats. json.dumps writes a tuple as an array, but the assertion skipped tuples, so a float held in a tuple would have been hashed unchecked. The docstring's equivalence of json.dumps(sort_keys=True) with RFC 8785 JCS, which sorts keys by UTF-16 code units, needs ASCII keys, and nothing asserted that. No hashed value had either form, so no printed value changes and vectors.json is byte-identical.
